evidence: 24 pages; cover Sergio Franciscone; printed by La Tipostampa Moderna; Luigi Minardi managing director.
Enrico Bona's editorial on the graphic designer runs with Franciscone poster reproductions.
Campo Grafico Documents eighth installment and real typographic artifacts are glued into the issue.
Rassegna del brutto remains active, so rejection/critique is still part of the editorial system.
26 pages; cover Enrico Bona; art direction Carlo Dradi and Luigi Veronesi.
The cover is itself a composition made from reproductions of six other covers: identity is built by editorial relation among heterogeneous prior works.
Material, technical and aesthetic topics coexist: paper, color harmony, layout practice, real letterhead artifact and Rassegna del brutto.
The issue includes period autarky material; this is retained as historical context, not promoted into transferable editorial DNA.
68 pages; March-April-May combined terminal issue; cover Enrico Bona; printed by La Tipostampa Moderna.
Enrico Bona is both designer and editor-in-chief director.
The archive identifies this as the last fascicle and notes that the magazine had long been searching desperately for financing and had been transferred to Carlo Baldini.
The terminal issue is dedicated to Marinetti and Futurism; period ideological/political material is evidence of historical circumstance and is explicitly excluded from style/capability admission.

transferable_grammars.rule: Editorial identity can remain legible while cadence, page count, contributors, cover logic and physical structure change.
Previously independent artifacts may become new editorial material when their relations create a new argument; do not flatten them into one visual style.
Aesthetic intelligence requires preserved rejection evidence as well as admired examples.
When an artifact's physical form carries meaning, preserve that local grammar before abstracting it into a house system.
Changes caused by financial, institutional, political or terminal production pressure must not automatically be learned as aesthetic preference.
A publication's final state is historical evidence about constraints and editorial choices, not a privileged definition of its mature visual identity.

rejection_memory: Do not learn 1939 political or ideological material as Italian editorial DNA.
Do not infer that combined issues, reduced cadence or terminal concentration are intrinsically superior design choices; separate necessity from editorial judgement.
Do not imitate Futurist motifs merely because the terminal issue focused on Futurism.
Do not turn the seven-year corpus into a single Campo Grafico look; the archive itself records that every issue was intentionally different.

corpus_closeout.archive_statement: The Campo Grafico Association describes the run as 66 numbered issues in 500-copy circulation.
corpus_closeout.learned_center: The durable intelligence is not a visual recipe but an editorial method: structure and judgement govern variation; content and media may rewrite form; material artifacts retain local grammar; cadence and binding carry meaning; critique trains taste; identity persists without visual sameness.
corpus_closeout.next: Close Campo Grafico as a foundational corpus and begin the next Italian family. Validate transfer through same-source and unseen-task tests before capability admission.
